business_problem: CSX needed to move a mission-critical railroad operations portal from on-premises MongoDB to MongoDB Atlas on Azure without disrupting 24/7 train operations or losing near real-time visibility for field teams.
solution_summary: CSX migrated its Railroad Transportation Operations Portal (RTOP) from on-premises MongoDB Enterprise Advanced to MongoDB Atlas on Azure with help from MongoDB Professional Services and Cluster-to-cluster Sync (mongosync). After a little more than two months of planning, the team used continuous synchronization between source and target databases so the cutover could happen in a matter of hours while RTOP stayed available to users across the rail network. On Atlas, RTOP acts as a centralized monitoring and alerting system that processes continuous train data streams, drives a map-based interface for field managers and leaders, and flags delays or staffing issues in near real time. The managed Atlas platform removes database overhead while giving CSX rapid scaling, higher availability, and a repeatable migration pattern for future applications.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Hosts RTOP on Azure and provides the managed operational data store for near real-time railroad monitoring and alerts.

solution_components.name: Cluster-to-cluster Sync (mongosync)
solution_components.role: Continuously synchronized source and target databases during the migration so RTOP could cut over with minimal disruption.

data_flow: Continuous train operations data flows into RTOP on MongoDB Atlas, where the platform analyzes events in near real time, generates alerts about delays or staffing issues, and serves map-based visibility to field managers and leadership across the network.
business_outcome: CSX completed a high-stakes migration in hours instead of risking a long outage, reduced database management overhead, improved scalability for operational workloads, and created a modernization blueprint for other critical systems.
